title: Why Is My Garbage Disposal Making Loud or Grinding Noises?
desc: Loud noises coming from your garbage disposal can mean it's jammed. Learn to safely look for signs it needs repair, plus when to call a plumber.

blocks.text: A garbage disposal is one of the most convenient appliances in a modern kitchen, but when it starts making strange noises, it can be alarming. Loud grinding, rattling, or humming sounds usually indicate that something is stuck, a part is loose, or the appliance is malfunctioning.

For San Antonio homeowners, it’s crucial to address these noises promptly. Ignoring them can allow a small issue to escalate into a serious jam, a damaging leak, or complete motor failure, leading to more complex and costly plumbing problems.

Understanding the potential causes behind these sounds is the first step toward finding a solution. This guide will help you decipher what your garbage disposal is trying to tell you, what safe initial steps you can take, and when it’s time to call in a professional plumber for help.
Common Reasons a Garbage Disposal Makes Loud Noises

A noisy garbage disposal is a clear sign that something is wrong inside the appliance. The specific sound it makes can often point to the root of the problem. Most issues stem from foreign objects, wear and tear, or improper use.

items: Tough or fibrous food scraps
Foreign objects like utensils or bones
Loose components like screws or lugs
Worn-down blades or impellers
A failing motor or worn-out bearings
Incorrect installation causing vibration
Not enough water during operation

blocks.text: What Different Disposal Noises Can Mean
Your garbage disposal communicates problems through sound. By learning to identify these noises, you can better understand what’s happening inside the unit and what steps to take next.

items: Grinding or scraping from trapped metal or glass
Rattling from small objects or loose bolts
Humming without grinding, which indicates a jam
Loud vibration from a loose mounting assembly
Persistent metallic noises from a broken part

blocks.text: What to Do First When Your Disposal Sounds Wrong

When your disposal starts making a racket, stop using it. Continuing to run a noisy disposal can cause permanent damage. There are a few safe steps you can take to assess the situation before calling for professional help.

items: Turn off the disposal at the wall switch.
Unplug the unit, or turn off its circuit breaker.
Use a flashlight to look for the obstruction.
Remove visible objects with pliers or tongs.
Restore power, and test the unit briefly.
Avoid using chemical drain cleaners.

blocks.text: When the Disposal May Be Jammed

A jam is one of the most frequent issues homeowners face with disposals. It happens when something, usually a hard food item or a non-food object, lodges itself between the impeller blade and the grinding chamber wall, preventing the unit from spinning.

A jammed disposal will typically make a distinct humming sound. This is the sound of the motor receiving power but being unable to turn. Turn off the unit right away if you hear this sound. Continuing to run a jammed disposal can cause the motor to overheat and burn out, turning a simple fix into a necessary replacement.

Many disposals have a small red or black reset button on the bottom of the unit that may pop out when it overheats. After clearing the jam and letting the motor cool, you may be able to press this button to restore power. However, if jams are occurring regularly or you cannot easily clear the obstruction, it is best to have a plumber handle it to avoid damaging the appliance.
Could the Garbage Disposal Need Repair or Replacement?

Sometimes, loud noises are a symptom of a deeper problem that a simple fix cannot resolve. If your disposal is getting on in years or showing multiple signs of failure, it might be time for a professional repair or a full replacement.

items: More than 10 years old with frequent jams
Persistent noises after clearing debris
Water leaking from the unit’s housing
A motor that struggles, shuts off, or won’t reset
Poor performance, odors, and clogs needing drain cleaning services
Repeated repairs becoming less cost-effective

blocks.text: How to Prevent Loud Disposal Noises

The best way to deal with a noisy garbage disposal is to prevent the problem from occurring in the first place. Proper use and regular maintenance can extend the life of your appliance and keep it running quietly and efficiently.

items: Run cold water before, during, and after use.
Feed the disposal food scraps slowly.
Avoid hard, fibrous, or greasy items.
Clean the appliance regularly with ice and citrus peels.
Do not overload the unit.
Schedule inspections for recurring problems.
